steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat, and stir in the ground beef and onion. Cook until the beef is crumbly, evenly browned, and no longer pink. Drain, and discard any excess grease.

Pour the beef mixture into a 3-quart casserole dish. Layer the sauerkraut over the ground beef, pour the tomato juice over the sauerkraut, then sprinkle with brown sugar. Bake in the preheated oven until the sauce is bubbly, about 60 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: BBQ Sauerkraut Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Baking mellows the sauerkraut in this hamburger casserole, and gives it a sweet BBQ flavor.
raw_recipe.name: BBQ Sauerkraut Casserole

review.reviewBody: Awesome recipe. It was sweet but VERY yummy. I was stumped as to what to serve with it so I just went with the BBQ normals, potatoe salad and mac and cheese. By the end my husband and I both mixed it with the mac and cheese and it was even better! Great by its self also!!

Browned the beef in an iron skillet and then used that as my casserole dish. The only thing I changed was using some mild homemade salsa as my tomato sauce and mixing the brown sugar in with it instead of sprinkling it on top. And I only baked it for 30 minutes at 400 F. I served it over rice. My husband really liked it and went back for seconds.

Made tonight and is very good. With all the reviews on being too sweet, only used about a quarter cup of brown sugar and drizzled with soy sauce to counter the sweetness. Also substituted tomato sauce with spaghetti sauce diluted with water. Last change was adding shredded Swiss during the last ten minutes of cooking. The recipe did not specify if you drain the sourkrout or not, I did not drain. instead I drizzled the juice as I spread it out before cooking. Will definately make again.

wonderful difference from the normal.....
used smaller can of sauerkraut and 3/4 c. brown sugar, added pinch of allspice, touch of basil and 2 cloves minced garlic with salt and pepper to taste. Served over baked onion/potato pierogies with some shredded cheese on top...will make again

I always like trying some “old-time” recipes from either my childhood or what would have maybe been popular in my parents time growing up. Most times, they have very little seasonings and require very basic ingredients - which was common for the time period. While there are some possible ratio issues with this, we found it to be very good and it did resemble a BBQ taste. I used 1 12oz can of tomato juice than 2c - which makes this runny enough but, if served over parboiled smashed potatoes? Maybe you want more of the juice to soak in. The brown sugar - as many pointed out - can be cut but half. But, it does make a nice crust on top. I wanted to make this more a one dish meal and I had less than a cup of leftover Ditalini pasta that I added on the meat before the sauerkraut. I also wanted to use up the last of my cherry tomatoes before they went bad so threw that in too. Baked 40 min at 375 to speed meal to table. I think I will try over potatoes sometime but I also think adding some egg noodles into the bake worked well too. Overall quick and economical meal! Thanks flbeachturtle!!
This was to die for. I just put it all in the crockpot and let it rip. Used stevia instead of brown sugar. Yummmmy!

I made this twice. first time with turkey meat and it was excellent. second time with beef and tried to double the recipe which lost it's greatness. Today I'm trying a vegetarian version with mash-potatoes instead of meat...
Yum, I really liked this recipe :) I didn't have any tomato juice so I used clamato instead and it worked out well :) I also added a packet of onion soup mix just because I love that stuff!

Super simple and delicious! It's not something that I would have thought of, but I knew I had hamburger and sauerkraut that I needed to used... so figured it was worth a try! Now it's something I'll make more often.

This was actually really good, I didn't have brown sugar so I improvised and used a dash of grape jelly and caramelized it with the ground beef, I also added diced tomatoes.
Good stuff! =)

Very easy to make and easy clean up after. I am vegetarian so did not try it. However most people I served it to liked it. One said "very good" as he took another big bite and nodded his head up and down, one said "yeah, pretty good" and finally one said "good flavor but a little dry, could use more sauce". So there you have it.
Thought this was just OK. I might cut back a little on the sauerkraut to beef ratio. It was a little sweet.

I thought the recipe was great! Super easy, yet tasty. My husband and I both loved it. My children, on the other hand, did not (age 18mos and 3 yrs). I also added a little more tomato sauce but next time would maybe add a can of crushed or stewed tomatoes as well. Thanks for the recipe!!!
Should have gone with my first instinct & totally avoided this recipe. WAY TOO SWEET!!! We love pork & sauerkraut stew, but did not care for this at all.

This was really easy to make. I thought it was pretty good, but my 3 teenage boys loved it and have asked me to make it again. Served it with homemade smashed potatoes. Filling meal, reminded me of meatloaf.
Not what I thought it would be. Sounded very good, but just wasn't something my husband or I liked. Too much sweetness for us.

This was surprisingly good! My grandmother used to make saurkraut with brown sugar so I didn't think this recipe would be sour like saurkraut is, but when my picky 6 year old said that I better make it again - I was in for a surprise! What an affordable dinner choice.
